relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-cluster-edit
relations.evidence: Specifies the port for the Couchbase Server Administration Console. Defaults to port 8091.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-cluster-edit
relations.evidence: Sets the data service memory quota (in MiB). This quota will be assigned to all future nodes added to the cluster with the data service.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-cluster-edit
relations.evidence: Sets the index service memory quota (in MiB). This parameter is required if the index service is specified in the --services option.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-cluster-edit
relations.evidence: Sets the full-text service memory quota (in MiB). This parameter is required if the full-text service is specified in the --services option.

notable_absence.finding: cluster-edit.md lets an operator change the built-in administrator username and password, the cluster-manager listen port, and three service memory quotas - a highly privileged set of operations - yet the page states no RBAC role or permission requirement anywhere, not even a generic pointer to a permissions overview. This matches the same absence already flagged on the couchbase-cli.md landing page: the CLI tree as a whole does not signpost which role a given subcommand needs, even for subcommands (like this one) that alter cluster-wide administrator credentials.

cross_component_finding: cluster-edit.md's own OPTIONS section is a near-verbatim copy of cluster-init.md's OPTIONS text for --cluster-fts-ramsize and --cluster-index-ramsize, down to the identical sentence 'This parameter is required if the full-text/index service is specified in the --services option' - but cluster-edit's own SYNOPSIS has no --services flag at all (cluster-init's does). The dangling reference to a flag the command doesn't have is a direct, checkable copy-paste artifact from one sibling subcommand's reference page to another, exactly the failure mode this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis predicted for lighter-reviewed, engineer-authored CLI pages.
cross_product_finding: No cross-product signal on this page - it documents a self-managed Couchbase Server CLI operation (editing cluster-manager credentials/port/quotas) with no stated or implied Capella analog; Capella clusters are not administered through this CLI. Absence noted plainly rather than forced.
